marie: FYI ran a perf pass on the nightly with HEAD at c5f3. Seeing a small but consistent latency regression for short chat requests when prefix caching is enabled. Digging in now.
ajay: what magnitude? p50/p95?
marie: p50 up ~6ms, p95 up ~18-22ms for short-turns (<64 new tokens). Throughput steady. Repro with local bench.
devon: interesting — prefix cache should reduce decode work. any kernel selection differences in the traces?
marie: yes — when prefix cache hits, we end up sending much shorter remaining lengths but the batcher groups them with regular requests. Kernel chooser then picks the mid-sized GEMM kernel tuned for 128 sequence because of the mixed batch length distribution. That kernel is heavier on register pressure on Ampere and gives worse latency for tiny sequences.
song: so prefix hits are changing the effective remaining-seq distribution. are we logging remaining_seq when batching?
marie: we log total_seq and kv_hit boolean but the batcher only uses total_seq for packing. Not remaining_seq.
ajay: that would explain it. for hits we should compute remaining = total_seq - prefix_len_cached. If remaining_seq is small, prefer the small-seq kernel or dispatch to the low-latency path.
devon: also token budget heuristics need to consider cached tokens. Right now token_budget = sum(total_seq) cap. If many prefixes are cached, we're overestimating budget and pack larger batches that look good on paper but create kernel mismatch.
marie: exactly. I reproduced with a micro-bench: 1000 requests with 80% prefix hit; baseline batcher p95=110ms, with remaining-aware packing p95=88ms.
marie: profiling snippet (perf trace):
```
# hot path: runtime_dispatch -> select_kernel(seq_len=120) -> run_gemm(kernel=GEMM_MID)
# with remaining-aware pack: select_kernel(seq_len=24) -> run_gemm(kernel=GEMM_SMALL)
```
ajay: nice. Two immediate fixes we can try: (1) make batcher subtract cached_prefix_len when computing virtual_length for packing/slotting, (2) add a kernel-hint tag if >X% of requests in batch are remaining<Y.
song: I can add logging for remaining_seq and a histogram to Console so we can monitor rollout. quick patch: add remaining_seq field to trace payload, e.g. `"remaining_seq": total_seq - cache.prefix_len`.
devon: also consider a fallback policy: if selected kernel is mid and batch mean remaining_seq < 32, trigger a re-eval to pick the small kernel. cheap check before launch.
ajay: agreed. Could be a fast path: preflight sample N items and choose kernel based on median remaining. avoids full reorder.
marie: will prototype remaining-aware virtual_length change in the packer. I'll push a branch and run the bench we used.
perf-bot: perf-experiment queued: exp/2026/prefill-aware-01, bench target 10k samples, compare p50/p95/p99 and throughput.
song: config sketch for packer (WIP):
```
{"packer": {
  "use_remaining_seq": true,
  "token_budget_mode": "remaining_sum",
  "kernel_hint_thresholds": {"small": 32, "mid": 96}
}}
```
marie: initial bench results on dev GPU: p95 down 20% for short-turns, throughput unchanged. I'll post numbers after one more run.
devon: also add a canary rollout flag in runtime so Dedicated customers can opt-out for now. No surprises in enterprise SLAs.
ajay: test matrix: varying prefix_hit_ratio {0,25,50,75,90}, model seq distribution, and hw gen (A100, A10G). We should see crossover point where remaining-aware beats baseline.
song: I'll add dashboard tiles: remaining_seq histogram, kernel_selected breakdown, batch_composition by remaining quantiles.
marie: next steps: PR for packer change (marie), kernel-hint preflight (ajay), dashboards (song), canary flag + perf experiment (devon).
devon: assign reviewers: ajay + song. timeline: aim for small canary next Tue.
marie: thanks team, will update thread with PR and perf links. :thumbsup:
